reason: ClickBench loads 100,000, 1,000,000, and 10,000,000 rows at SF 0.1, 1, and 10, and BigQuery scans 0.690 GB, 5.171 GB, and 51.713 GB. Despite the 100x row increase and 74.98x scanned-byte increase, the geometric mean grows 1.45x and the median per-query mean grows 1.38x. Query caching is recorded off, measurement runs at 0.89 to 0.94 of warmup, and all 43 queries succeed. Measured client statement overhead is 364 to 408 ms against query geometric means of 712 to 1,033 ms, while six heavier queries grow at least 2x. This is consistent with fixed job and client overhead dominating the lighter queries rather than cached results or a scale/data-volume defect; provider queue and execution phases were not captured.
